content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Classification: deviation (fallback target).**

- **What exists:** § 14.2(B) contains an M&I indemnity with an express duty to defend and third-party IP infringement coverage (US patent, copyright, trademark), and § 14.3 supplies the notice, control-of-defence and cooperation mechanics. § 6.4/21.4 and 14.2(A) indemnities were also reviewed.
- **Why it fails fallback:** (i) no infringement remedies at all — nothing requires M&I to procure continued use, modify or replace, or to refund fees if those fail; (ii) no super-cap — § 13.4 begins "Notwithstanding any provision in this Agreement" and caps M&I's total liability, including the indemnity, at three months' payments, far below 3× annual fees.
- **Cure (two surgical ops):** a new § 14.2(C) carrying procure/modify/replace-or-refund plus a 3× annual fees cap on Paragraph B, and a conforming lead-in change in § 13.4 ("Except as provided in Section 14.2(C)") so the caps do not conflict.
- **Left alone:** the indemnity is unqualified by Customer modification/combination/specification exclusions (better than the fallback permits), so no exclusions were added; preferred-only items (affiliates, Vendor data-breach and gross-negligence heads, narrowing our own 14.2(A) indemnity) are noted in the rationale rather than drafted.
